from.place: Proof, paragraph checking (b), sentence: a continuous surjection from a compact space onto a Hausdorff space is closed and hence a quotient map.

title: Compact-to-Hausdorff surjections are quotient maps
statement: Let $X,Y$ be topological spaces and $U\subseteq X$, $V\subseteq Y$ subsets, endowed with their subspace topologies [def-kun-subspace-topology]. Suppose $U$ is quasi-compact (every open cover has a finite subcover) and $V$ is Hausdorff. Let $q:U\to V$ be continuous and surjective. Then $q$ is a quotient map: for every subset $W\subseteq V$, $W$ is open in $V$ if and only if $q^{-1}(W)$ is open in $U$. This includes the case $U=X$ and $V=Y$.
